### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e8f663710ccfe069138d0fe8ba1ccbd98111ed3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** `l1-face --pr 37791`: one flag, judged below. Check-runs at 99ccb26c6e: 57 success, 14 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; mergeable_state clean. Draft, `Fixes #37744`. 3 test files, +122/-0. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**The flag is not a gap.** `skip-changeset` covers three packages, and the only file in each is a test (`logger-error-cause.test.ts`, `loggers.test.ts`, `server-fault-log-cause.test.ts`). `core`, `observability` and `types` all ship `dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing published moves. Both premises hold: the diff is test-only, and no shipped file changes.

**Fixes is right.**
- N1, two directions: each package now reads its own source file and pins both lists (the default redact words, `CONCATENATED_SECRET_QUALIFIERS`) to an exact set. The existing behaviour fixtures red a dropped word; the new pins red an added one. The ablation table shows all six one-word additions red in their own package.
- N2: both branches have fixtures in every parity block (types `faultCauseChain`, core `ObjectLogger`, both observability loggers). The six branch ablations (stack branch made unconditional, `causeOf` limited to `Error`) each red their case.
- No runtime source line changes.

**Judged.**
- Reading the declaration out of source text with a regex is brittle on reformatting, but it fails loud (`toHaveLength(1)` on the match) and never passes silently. It is the form the card offered. Accepted.
- The object-cause fixture pins the current serialisation `{"code":"E4","cause":{}}`, so an `Error` nested inside it prints as `{}` on that line before the chain continues. That documents today's behaviour; the card asks only that the chain continue, which the second entry pins. Not filed.

**Contract review.** None owed.

**Landing:** not governed, ≤3000 lines, no narrowing. The area lands it. `Fixes` closes the card.
